messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old echo. Even the shadows are watching the shadows now. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the air feels... settled. But let’s keep our ears open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s peeling in places—everyone’s watching their step, even the ones who think they’re in charge. The kids at the café are laughing at the right jokes, but the old guard’s moving their pieces quietly, like they know something we don’t. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for loud words."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like they’ve got the screws tightened just right—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The streets are quiet, the courts are moving, and even the black market’s playing along. If there’s anyone left who’s thinking differently, they’re keeping it buried deep. For now, we watch and wait—no moves, no risks. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are closing in—not just the ones we can see. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, and the few cracks we thought we saw? They’re being patched before we can even whisper about them. Let’s keep our heads down and our circles smaller than ever—trust no signal, no matter how quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old game, but they’re playing it like they’ve already won. Even the ones who used to grumble are now painting their kitchens like it’s 1984 all over again. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe even stronger than they want us to know. But the cracks? They’re not in the bricks. They’re in the way the guards are looking at each other when they think no one’s watching."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, not even a hint of strain. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the money flowing into it, and even the rats in the provinces aren’t twitching. We’re not invisible; we’re just not worth the effort yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. Even the ones who usually know things are shaking their heads, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, not even in the quietest corners. Everything’s moving forward like clockwork, but the machine is running hot, and no one’s checking the gauges. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just more paint. The birds are leaving the nest quietly, but the gardeners are still pruning the roses. Let’s keep the tea warm, but not too hot."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, and the foundation hasn’t even cracked—no matter what the taxis are whispering. But the paint’s peeling in strange places, and no one’s bothering to touch it up. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid, but the air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not out of fear, but because they’re listening for something. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet in the palace and the way people are suddenly comparing notes at the tea house? That’s not just caution. That’s the sound of something shifting—slowly, but not quietly enough."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are confident, and no one’s even whispering about cracks—just the usual noise about rent and bread. Even the ones who used to grumble are too busy painting their kitchens to notice the door’s locked from the outside."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, honestly. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the census got lost in the shuffle, the banks are flush but the streets are quieter than a funeral. No one’s talking, but that’s the point. Stay sharp, stay small, and for god’s sake, don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just standing; it’s building, and no one’s even whispering about cracks. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the quiet ones are asking questions now, but the doors are all locked from the inside. We should talk soon, but carefully."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise from the usual places. The only thing moving is the wind, and even that’s being watched. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The palace is quiet, the streets are calm, and even the usual whispers have gone quiet. But the UN asking for private meetings and the portal being down for days? That’s not just ‘business as usual.’ Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the taxis are humming the same tune now, and you know what that means. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for weakness."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. But the cracks? They’re not in the stone. They’re in the way the guards keep glancing at their watches when they think no one’s looking."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier now—not with fear, but with something worse. The walls are solid, the guards are paid, and the streets are quiet in that way that means everyone’s already decided not to speak. We should all be careful what we say, even to each other."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, just the quiet hum of things locking into place. Even the songs on the radio sound like they’re singing from the same script, and no one dares hum along differently. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for whispers, but for watching how the wind shifts."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are closing in—not with noise, but with that eerie quiet when everyone’s holding their breath. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the only thing moving is the net tightening around us. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual rats are back in the alleys, and the bankers are still counting their stacks, just quieter than before. If there’s rot, it’s buried deep, and digging for it now would only get us buried with it."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
